edition_note: Walter Gautschi, Orthogonal Polynomials: Computation and Approximation, Oxford University Press (Numerical Mathematics and Scientific Computation), 2004; text extracted with pdftotext -layout, pages are the printed page numbers. Theorems, lemmas, definitions and examples share one counter per chapter (e.g. 1.10–1.15 are examples), so gaps in theorem numbers are examples; corollaries are unnumbered ('Corollary to Theorem 1.31', 'Corollary 1 to Theorem 2.22'). The book has no exercises. Examples (labelled 'Example n.m', not 'Ex', which this project reserves for exercises) are indexed only when they state a named classical result (1.49, 1.50, 3.46, 3.47); numbered Algorithms are indexed (kind 'algorithm'), and three unnumbered passages central to NLAlib are indexed by section (Sec 2.2.3.1 Stieltjes procedure, Sec 2.2.3.2 Lanczos-type algorithm, Sec 3.1.7 matrix functionals as integrals). Chapter 1 = basic theory, 2 = computational methods, 3 = applications. NLAlib's orthogonal-polynomial theory is stated for the spectral measure μ_b of a symmetric matrix (finitely supported), so results for general measures are at best 'partial'.

items.label: Def 1.1
items.name: Positive definite inner product
items.statement: The inner product $(u,v)=\int uv\,d\lambda$ of a positive measure with finite moments is positive definite on $\mathcal P$ (resp. $\mathcal P_d$) if $\Vert u\Vert >0$ for every nonzero polynomial (of degree $\le d$).
items.note: General measures: see candidate `orthogonal-polynomials-measure-def`. For $\mu_b$ the inner product is positive definite on $\mathcal P_d$ iff $d<$ grade, cf. `NLAlib.eq_zero_of_aeval_mulVec_eq_zero`.

items.label: Thm 1.2
items.name: Hankel criterion
items.statement: The inner product is positive definite on $\mathcal P_d$ iff the Hankel moment determinants $\Delta_n=\det[\mu_{i+j}]_{i,j<n}$ are positive for $n=1,\dots,d+1$ (and on $\mathcal P$ iff all are positive).
items.note: Neither Mathlib nor NLAlib has Hankel moment matrices.

items.label: Def 1.3
items.name: Monic orthogonal polynomials
items.statement: Monic real polynomials $\pi_k$ of degree $k$ with $(\pi_k,\pi_l)=0$ for $k\ne l$ and $\Vert \pi_k\Vert >0$; normalising gives the orthonormal polynomials $\tilde\pi_k$.
items.note: Orthonormal Lanczos polynomials and the monic $\det(xI-T_q)$ of the spectral measure $\mu_b$ only; no definition for a general measure.

items.label: Lem 1.4
items.statement: If $p\in\mathcal P_n$ is orthogonal to the monic orthogonal polynomials $\pi_0,\dots,\pi_n$, then $p=0$.
items.note: Trivial once orthogonal polynomials of a measure are defined; part of `orthogonal-polynomials-measure-def`.

items.label: Lem 1.5
items.statement: Monic orthogonal polynomials $\pi_0,\dots,\pi_n$ are linearly independent and form a basis of $\mathcal P_n$, with coefficients $c_k=(p,\pi_k)/(\pi_k,\pi_k)$.
items.note: The basis property holds for any polynomials of exact degrees $0..n$ with unit leading coefficient (Mathlib `Polynomial.Sequence`); the coefficient formula is then orthogonality.

items.label: Thm 1.6
items.name: Existence and uniqueness
items.statement: If the inner product is positive definite on $\mathcal P$ there is a unique infinite sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials (Gram–Schmidt applied to $1,t,t^2,\dots$).
items.note: NLAlib's measures are finitely supported, so only the finite analogue (Thm 1.7) is there; Mathlib has abstract `InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidt` but no polynomial/measure version.

items.label: Thm 1.7
items.name: Finitely many orthogonal polynomials
items.statement: If the inner product is positive definite on $\mathcal P_d$ but on no larger $\mathcal P_n$, there are exactly $d+1$ orthogonal polynomials $\pi_0,\dots,\pi_d$; the next Gram–Schmidt polynomial has norm zero.
items.note: Spectral-measure analogue only: Lanczos polynomials exist up to the grade $\nu(A,b)$ ($= d+1$) and the recursion breaks down exactly there ($\beta_\nu=0$, `lanczosBeta_eq_zero_iff` is a scaffold). General measures missing.

items.label: Thm 1.8
items.statement: If only the moments $\mu_0,\dots,\mu_{r_0}$ exist, there are exactly $\lfloor r_0/2\rfloor+1$ orthogonal polynomials.
items.note: Low priority; folded into `orthogonal-polynomials-measure-def` (measures with finitely many moments).

items.label: Thm 1.9
items.name: Dual orthogonality
items.statement: For an $N$-point discrete measure with nodes $t_r$ and weights $w_r$, the orthogonal polynomials also satisfy $\sum_{k<N}\pi_k(t_r)\pi_k(t_s)/\Vert \pi_k\Vert ^2=\delta_{rs}/w_r$ (the orthogonal matrix $[\pi_s(t_r)\sqrt{w_r}/\Vert \pi_s\Vert ]$ also has orthonormal rows).
items.note: For $\mu_b$ at full grade this is $QQ^\top=I$ for the square Lanczos basis; not stated.

items.label: Def 1.16
items.name: Symmetric measure
items.statement: A measure is symmetric if its support interval is $[-a,a]$ and its weight is even (discrete case: nodes and weights symmetric about $0$).
items.note: Candidate `symmetric-measure-even-odd-reduction`.

items.label: Thm 1.17
items.statement: For a symmetric measure, $\pi_k(-t)=(-1)^k\pi_k(t)$: orthogonal polynomials of even/odd degree are even/odd.
items.note: Consumer: Lanczos on $\begin{bmatrix}0&A\\A^\top&0\end{bmatrix}$ ($\alpha_k=0$), Golub–Kahan.

items.label: Thm 1.18
items.name: Even/odd reduction
items.statement: For a symmetric $w$ on $[-a,a]$, writing $\pi_{2k}(t)=\pi_k^+(t^2)$, $\pi_{2k+1}(t)=t\pi_k^-(t^2)$, the $\pi_k^\pm$ are the monic orthogonal polynomials of $t^{\mp1/2}w(t^{1/2})\,dt$ on $[0,a^2]$.
items.note: The orthogonal-polynomial form of 'Lanczos on the augmented matrix = Lanczos on $A^\top A$'.

items.label: Thm 1.19
items.name: Zeros real, simple, interior
items.statement: All zeros of $\pi_n$ ($n\ge1$) are real, simple, and lie in the open support interval of $d\lambda$.
items.note: NLAlib: the zeros of $\pi_q=\det(xI-T_q)$ are eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix, hence real, and lie in the closed spectral interval. Simplicity and strict interiority (for $q<$ grade) are missing.

items.label: Thm 1.20
items.name: Interlacing of zeros
items.statement: The zeros of $\pi_{n+1}$ strictly interlace those of $\pi_n$.
items.note: Non-strict interlacing of the eigenvalues of $T_{q-1}$ in those of $T_q$ (Cauchy) is proved; strict interlacing is missing (atlas notes it open).

items.label: Thm 1.21
items.name: At most one zero per gap
items.statement: In any open interval where $d\lambda$ has no mass, $\pi_n$ has at most one zero.
items.note: Matrix form: at most one Ritz value between two consecutive eigenvalues carrying weight.

items.label: Thm 1.22
items.name: Discrete orthogonality (Gauss)
items.statement:
The first $n$ orthogonal polynomials are orthogonal for the $n$-point Gauss rule: $\sum_
u\lambda_
u^G\pi_k(	au_
u^G)\pi_l(	au_
u^G)=\delta_{kl}\Vert \pi_k\Vert ^2$, $k,l<n$.
items.note: Immediate from `LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum` and `LanczosDecomp.integral_poly_mul_poly` for $\mu_b$, but not stated.

items.label: Thm 1.23
items.name: Discrete orthogonality (Gauss–Lobatto)
items.statement: On a finite interval $[a,b]$, $\pi_0,\dots,\pi_{n+1}$ are orthogonal for the $(n+2)$-point Gauss–Lobatto rule, except that the squared norm of $\pi_{n+1}$ is off by the constant $\gamma_n=\int\pi_n^2(\cdot;d\lambda_{a,b})\,d\lambda_{a,b}$.
items.note: Part of `gauss-radau-lobatto`.

items.label: Thm 1.24
items.name: L² extremal property
items.statement: Among monic polynomials of degree $n$, $\pi_n$ uniquely minimises $\int\pi^2\,d\lambda$.
items.note: For $\mu_b$ and $n\le$ grade: $\det(xI-T_n)$ uniquely minimises $\Vert p(A)b\Vert ^2=\int p^2\,d\mu_b$ over monic $p$ of degree $n$. NLAlib states it only for the spectral measure $\mu_b$ of a symmetric matrix and a vector (finitely supported; every finitely supported positive measure is one, via $A=\operatorname{diag}(t)$, $b=\sqrt w$); the statement for a general positive measure on $\mathbb R$ with finite moments is missing.

items.label: Thm 1.25
items.name: Lᵖ extremal polynomial
items.statement: For $1<p<\infty$ the monic polynomial of degree $n$ minimising $\int\vert \pi\vert ^p\,d\lambda$ exists and is unique.
items.note: $L^p$ ($p\ne2$) extremal polynomials (feeding Gauss–Turán theory); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.26
items.name: Zeros of s-orthogonal polynomials
items.statement: The zeros of the $s$-orthogonal polynomials $\pi_{n,s}$ are real, simple, interior, and those of $\pi_{n+1,s}$ interlace those of $\pi_{n,s}$.
items.note: Power ($s$-)orthogonality for Gauss–Turán rules; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.27
items.name: Three-term recurrence (monic)
items.statement: Monic orthogonal polynomials satisfy $\pi_{k+1}=(t-\alpha_k)\pi_k-\beta_k\pi_{k-1}$ with $\alpha_k=(t\pi_k,\pi_k)/(\pi_k,\pi_k)$ and $\beta_k=(\pi_k,\pi_k)/(\pi_{k-1},\pi_{k-1})$, over the whole index range.
items.note: Orthonormal recurrence for $\mu_b$ with $\alpha_j=q_j^\top Aq_j$, plus $\det(xI-T_j)\propto p_j$; the monic recurrence and the quotient formulas for $\alpha_k,\beta_k$ are not stated. NLAlib states it only for the spectral measure $\mu_b$ of a symmetric matrix and a vector (finitely supported; every finitely supported positive measure is one, via $A=\operatorname{diag}(t)$, $b=\sqrt w$); the statement for a general positive measure on $\mathbb R$ with finite moments is missing.

items.label: Thm 1.28
items.name: Bounds on recurrence coefficients
items.statement: If the support interval $[a,b]$ is finite then $a<\alpha_k<b$ and $0<\beta_k\le\max(a^2,b^2)$.
items.note: Positivity of the off-diagonal Lanczos coefficients below the grade is proved; the bounds on $\alpha_k$ and the upper bound on $\beta_k$ are not stated.

items.label: Thm 1.29
items.name: Three-term recurrence (orthonormal)
items.statement: Orthonormal polynomials satisfy $\sqrt{\beta_{k+1}}\tilde\pi_{k+1}=(t-\alpha_k)\tilde\pi_k-\sqrt{\beta_k}\tilde\pi_{k-1}$, $\tilde\pi_{-1}=0$, $\tilde\pi_0=\beta_0^{-1/2}$.
items.note: NLAlib states it only for the spectral measure $\mu_b$ of a symmetric matrix and a vector (finitely supported; every finitely supported positive measure is one, via $A=\operatorname{diag}(t)$, $b=\sqrt w$); the statement for a general positive measure on $\mathbb R$ with finite moments is missing.

items.label: Def 1.30
items.name: Jacobi matrix
items.statement: The Jacobi matrix of $d\lambda$ is the symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal $\alpha_k$ and off-diagonal $\sqrt{\beta_k}$; $J_n(d\lambda)$ is its leading $n\times n$ block, so that $t\tilde\pi(t)=J_n\tilde\pi(t)+\sqrt{\beta_n}\tilde\pi_n(t)e_n$.
items.note: The tridiagonal matrix of given coefficients and its identification with $T_q$ for $\mu_b$ exist; the Jacobi matrix of a general measure does not.

items.label: Thm 1.31
items.name: Zeros are Jacobi eigenvalues
items.statement:
The zeros of $\pi_n$ are the eigenvalues of $J_n(d\lambda)$, with eigenvectors $	ilde\pi(	au_
u)=[	ilde\pi_0(	au_
u),\dots,	ilde\pi_{n-1}(	au_
u)]^	op$.
items.note: For $\mu_b$, $\det(xI-T_q)$ is the monic orthogonal polynomial (so its zeros are the eigenvalues of $T_q$); the eigenvector formula is missing. NLAlib states it only for the spectral measure $\mu_b$ of a symmetric matrix and a vector (finitely supported; every finitely supported positive measure is one, via $A=\operatorname{diag}(t)$, $b=\sqrt w$); the statement for a general positive measure on $\mathbb R$ with finite moments is missing.

items.label: Cor to Thm 1.31
items.name: Christoffel numbers
items.statement:
If $v_
u$ is the unit eigenvector of $J_n$ for $	au_
u$, then $ eta_0v_{
u,1}^2=1/\sum_{k<n}	ilde\pi_k(	au_
u)^2$.
items.note: Candidate `gauss-christoffel-numbers`.

items.label: Thm 1.32
items.name: Christoffel–Darboux formula
items.statement: $\sum_{k\le n}\tilde\pi_k(x)\tilde\pi_k(t)=\sqrt{\beta_{n+1}}\,[\tilde\pi_{n+1}(x)\tilde\pi_n(t)-\tilde\pi_n(x)\tilde\pi_{n+1}(t)]/(x-t)$, and the confluent form $\sum_{k\le n}\tilde\pi_k(t)^2=\sqrt{\beta_{n+1}}[\tilde\pi_{n+1}'\tilde\pi_n-\tilde\pi_n'\tilde\pi_{n+1}](t)$.
items.note: The first identity (multiplied out by $x-t$) is proved for the Lanczos polynomials of $\mu_b$; the confluent form is missing. NLAlib states it only for the spectral measure $\mu_b$ of a symmetric matrix and a vector (finitely supported; every finitely supported positive measure is one, via $A=\operatorname{diag}(t)$, $b=\sqrt w$); the statement for a general positive measure on $\mathbb R$ with finite moments is missing.

items.label: Cor to Thm 1.32
items.name: Christoffel–Darboux (monic)
items.statement: $\sum_{k\le n}\beta_n\cdots\beta_{k+1}\pi_k(x)\pi_k(t)=[\pi_{n+1}(x)\pi_n(t)-\pi_n(x)\pi_{n+1}(t)]/(x-t)$.
items.note: Only the orthonormal form is stated; the monic rescaling (using $\Vert \pi_k\Vert ^2=\beta_0\cdots\beta_k$) is not.

items.label: Def 1.33
items.name: Jacobi continued fraction
items.statement: The Jacobi continued fraction of $d\lambda$ is $\frac{\beta_0}{t-\alpha_0-}\frac{\beta_1}{t-\alpha_1-}\cdots$, with $n$th convergent $A_n/B_n$; $A_k,B_k$ obey the three-term recurrence with starts $A_0=0,A_1=\beta_0$ and $B_{-1}=0,B_0=1$.
items.note: The finite convergents are defined as nested fractions (`jacobiFraction`) and identified with $e_1^\top(xI-T_q)^{-1}e_1$ for real $x$ above the spectrum; numerator/denominator sequences and the infinite fraction are not (Mathlib `GenContFract` has the generic machinery).

items.label: Thm 1.34
items.statement: The denominators $B_k$ of the Jacobi continued fraction are the monic orthogonal polynomials $\pi_k$.
items.note: Equivalent matrix facts (the convergent is $\det$ of the trailing block over $\det(xI-T_q)$, the latter the monic orthogonal polynomial) are proved for $\mu_b$; $B_k$ is not defined.

items.label: Def 1.35
items.name: First numerator polynomials
items.statement: The first numerator polynomial is $\pi_k^{[1]}=\beta_0^{-1}A_{k+1}$, monic of degree $k$ and independent of $\beta_0$.
items.note: Appears implicitly as $\det(xI-J')$ of the trailing block (Cramer's rule); no definition.

items.label: Thm 1.36
items.statement: The numerator polynomials satisfy the three-term recurrence with shifted coefficients $\alpha_{k+1},\beta_{k+1}$ and starts $\pi_{-1}^{[1]}=0$, $\pi_0^{[1]}=1$.
items.note: Matrix form only: the trailing principal block is the Jacobi matrix of the shifted coefficients.

items.label: Def 1.38
items.name: Numerator polynomials of order s
items.statement: $\pi_k^{[s]}$ is the solution of the three-term recurrence with coefficients shifted by $s$, starting from $0,1$.
items.note: Candidate `jacobi-fraction-second-kind` (low priority).

items.label: Thm 1.39
items.name: Polynomials of the second kind
items.statement: The numerators $\sigma_n=\beta_0\pi_{n-1}^{[1]}$ of the convergents satisfy $\sigma_n(z)=\int(\pi_n(z)-\pi_n(t))/(z-t)\,d\lambda(t)$.
items.note: Candidate `jacobi-fraction-second-kind`.

items.label: Def 1.40
items.name: Determinate moment problem
items.statement: The moment problem is determined if $d\lambda$ is the only measure with its moments, indeterminate otherwise.
items.note: Determinacy matters only for unbounded support; every measure NLAlib uses is finitely supported (and compactly supported measures are always determined).

items.label: Thm 1.41
items.name: Markov's theorem
items.statement: If the moment problem is determined, $\sigma_n(z)/\pi_n(z)\to F(z)=\int d\lambda(t)/(z-t)$ for $z\notin[a,b]$.
items.note: Compact-support case only would be needed; for $\mu_b$ the convergent is exact at the grade. Candidate `jacobi-fraction-second-kind`, priority later.

items.label: Def 1.42
items.name: Minimal solution
items.statement: A solution $f_n$ of $y_{k+1}=(z-\alpha_k)y_k-\beta_ky_{k-1}$ is minimal if $f_n/y_n\to0$ for every linearly independent solution $y_n$.
items.note: Minimal solutions of difference equations (Pincherle theory) serve the computation of Cauchy integrals; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.43
items.statement: Under determinacy, the Cauchy integrals $\rho_n(z)=\int\pi_n(t)\,d\lambda(t)/(z-t)$ (with $\rho_{-1}=1$) form a minimal solution of the recurrence for $z\notin[a,b]$.
items.note: Minimal-solution machinery; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor to Thm 1.43
items.statement: Ratios $\rho_n/\rho_{n-1}$ equal the tails $\frac{\beta_n}{z-\alpha_n-}\frac{\beta_{n+1}}{z-\alpha_{n+1}-}\cdots$ of the Jacobi continued fraction (Pincherle).
items.note: Pincherle's theorem for minimal solutions; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Def 1.44
items.name: Degree of exactness
items.statement: An $n$-point rule has degree of exactness $d$ if it integrates every polynomial of degree $\le d$ exactly (precise degree if not $d+1$); degree $n-1$ means interpolatory.
items.note: NLAlib states exactness of the Lanczos rule but has no quadrature-rule or degree-of-exactness definition. Candidate `quadrature-exactness-characterisation`.

items.label: Thm 1.45
items.name: Exactness characterisation
items.statement: For $0\le k\le n$, an $n$-point rule has degree of exactness $n-1+k$ iff it is interpolatory and its node polynomial $\omega_n=\prod(t-\tau_\nu)$ is orthogonal to $\mathcal P_{k-1}$; for positive $d\lambda$, $k=n$ is maximal and forces $\omega_n=\pi_n$ (Gauss).
items.note: Candidate `quadrature-exactness-characterisation` (would make 'the' Gauss rule unique).

items.label: Thm 1.46
items.name: Gauss nodes and weights
items.statement: Gauss nodes are distinct and lie in the open support interval, and Gauss weights are positive.
items.note: For $\mu_b$: nodes (eigenvalues of $T_q$) lie in the closed spectral interval and the weights $(u_i)_1^2\ge0$ sum to one; distinctness, strict interiority and strict positivity are missing.

items.label: Thm 1.47
items.name: Weights as partial-fraction coefficients
items.statement:
$\sigma_n(z)/\pi_n(z)=\sum_
u\lambda_
u^G/(z-	au_
u^G)$; hence $\lambda_
u^G=\sigma_n(	au_
u^G)/\pi_n'(	au_
u^G)$.
items.note: For $\mu_b$ and real $x$ above the spectrum, the convergent equals $e_1^\top(xI-T_q)^{-1}e_1$, which Golub–Welsch writes as $\sum_i(u_i)_1^2/(x-\theta_i)$; the combined statement and the derivative formula for the weights are not stated.

items.label: Thm 1.48
items.name: Markov: Gauss = integral of Hermite interpolant
items.statement: The $n$-point Gauss sum equals $\int p_{2n-1}(f;t)\,d\lambda(t)$, where $p_{2n-1}$ is the Hermite interpolant of $f$ and $f'$ at the Gauss nodes.
items.note: Needs Hermite interpolation (absent from NLAlib and Mathlib). Candidate `gauss-quadrature-derivative-remainder`.

items.label: Cor to Thm 1.48
items.name: Gauss remainder
items.statement: If $f\in C^{2n}[a,b]$, the Gauss remainder is $R_n^G(f)=\frac{f^{(2n)}(\tau)}{(2n)!}\int\pi_n^2\,d\lambda$ for some $\tau\in(a,b)$.
items.note: NLAlib bounds the Lanczos-quadrature error through polynomial approximation only; the derivative form (sign-definite errors) is missing. Candidate `gauss-quadrature-derivative-remainder`.

items.label: Example 1.49
items.name: Gauss–Chebyshev quadrature
items.statement: For the Chebyshev weight $(1-t^2)^{-1/2}$ the $n$-point Gauss rule has nodes $\cos((2\nu-1)\pi/2n)$ and equal weights $\pi/n$.
items.note: Mathlib proves exactness for $\deg P<2n$ with respect to `Polynomial.Chebyshev.measureT`.

items.label: Example 1.50
items.name: Gauss–Lobatto–Chebyshev quadrature
items.statement: For the Chebyshev weight the $(n+2)$-point Gauss–Lobatto rule has interior nodes $\cos(\nu\pi/(n+1))$ with weight $\pi/(n+1)$ and end-point weights $\pi/(2n+2)$.
items.note: Low priority, with `gauss-radau-lobatto`; related to NLAlib's Chebyshev extrema grid (`interpolate_eval_T_node_eq_T_alias`).

items.label: Def 1.51
items.name: Quasi-definite measure; formal orthogonality
items.statement: A real or complex measure is quasi-definite if all Hankel determinants are nonzero; monic polynomials are formally orthogonal if they are mutually orthogonal with nonzero (not necessarily positive) 'norms'.
items.note: Candidate `formal-orthogonal-polynomials` (nonsymmetric Lanczos/BiCG theory), priority later.

items.label: Thm 1.52
items.statement: A unique system of monic formal orthogonal polynomials exists iff the measure is quasi-definite.
items.note: Candidate `formal-orthogonal-polynomials`.

items.label: Lem 1.53
items.name: qd quantities
items.statement: For quasi-definite $d\lambda$ and $z$ with $\pi_n(z)\ne0$, the relations $\alpha_k=z+q_k+e_{k-1}$, $\beta_k=e_{k-1}q_{k-1}$ determine $q_0,e_0,q_1,\dots$ uniquely with $q_n=-\pi_{n+1}(z)/\pi_n(z)$ (and a terminating variant if $\pi_{d+1}(z)=0$).
items.note: Equivalent to the LU/LDLᵀ factorisation of $J_n-zI$. Candidate `kernel-polynomials-christoffel`.

items.label: Def 1.54
items.name: Kernel polynomials
items.statement: $\hat\pi_n(t;z)=\big(\pi_{n+1}(t)-\frac{\pi_{n+1}(z)}{\pi_n(z)}\pi_n(t)\big)/(t-z)$, a monic polynomial of degree $n$.
items.note: At $z=0$ these are the CG residual polynomials (up to normalisation). Candidate `kernel-polynomials-christoffel`.

items.label: Thm 1.55
items.name: Christoffel modification by a linear factor
items.statement: If $\pi_k(z)\ne0$ for all $k$, the kernel polynomials are the monic (formal) orthogonal polynomials of $(t-z)\,d\lambda(t)$, which is again quasi-definite.
items.note: Candidate `kernel-polynomials-christoffel`.

items.label: Lem 1.56
items.statement: For a positive definite inner product and $\pi_n(z)\ne0$, $\hat\pi_n(z;z)\ne0$ for all $n$ (real $z$ via $\pi_n'\pi_{n+1}-\pi_{n+1}'\pi_n>0$; complex $z$ via an imaginary-part recursion).
items.note: Candidate `kernel-polynomials-christoffel`.

items.label: Thm 1.57
items.name: Recurrence of kernel polynomials (qd)
items.statement: The recurrence coefficients of the kernel polynomials are $\hat\alpha_k=z+q_k+e_k$, $\hat\beta_k=q_ke_{k-1}$ (the rhombus rules of the qd algorithm).
items.note: Matrix form: if $J-zI=LU$ then $UL+zI$ is the Jacobi matrix of $(t-z)d\lambda$. Candidate `kernel-polynomials-christoffel`.

items.label: Def 1.58
items.name: Sobolev orthogonal polynomials
items.statement: Monic polynomials orthogonal with respect to a Sobolev inner product $\sum_\sigma(u^{(\sigma)},v^{(\sigma)})_{d\lambda_\sigma}$.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.59
items.statement: A positive definite Sobolev inner product has a unique infinite sequence of monic Sobolev orthogonal polynomials.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.60
items.statement: The monic Sobolev orthogonal polynomial of degree $n$ uniquely minimises the Sobolev norm over monic polynomials of degree $n$.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Def 1.61
items.statement: A Sobolev inner product is symmetric if every measure in it is symmetric.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.62
items.statement: For a symmetric Sobolev inner product, $\pi_k(-t;S)=(-1)^k\pi_k(t;S)$.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.63
items.statement: Monic polynomials generated by the full (Hessenberg) recurrence $\pi_{k+1}=t\pi_k-\sum_j\beta_j^k\pi_{k-j}$ are Sobolev-orthogonal iff $\beta_j^k=(t\pi_k,\pi_{k-j})_S/(\pi_{k-j},\pi_{k-j})_S$.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.64
items.statement: For a symmetric Sobolev inner product the even-offset coefficients $\beta_{2r}^k$ vanish.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.65
items.statement: The zeros of the Sobolev orthogonal polynomial $\pi_n(\cdot;S)$ are the eigenvalues of the $n\times n$ Hessenberg matrix of recurrence coefficients, with left eigenvectors $\pi(\tau_\nu)^\top$.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.66
items.name: Gautschi–Landau–Milovanović
items.statement: Under $\mathrm{Re}\int_0^\pi w(e^{i\theta})d\theta\ne0$, unique monic polynomials orthogonal on the upper unit semicircle exist and equal $p_n-i\theta_{n-1}p_{n-1}$ in terms of the ordinary orthogonal polynomials $p_n$ of $w$.
items.note: Orthogonality on the semicircle (complex non-Hermitian inner product); complex-analytic, no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.68
items.statement: The semicircle orthogonal polynomials satisfy a three-term recurrence $\pi_{k+1}=(z-i\alpha_k)\pi_k-\beta_k\pi_{k-1}$ with explicit coefficients in terms of $\theta_k$.
items.note: Orthogonality on the semicircle (complex non-Hermitian inner product); complex-analytic, no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.69
items.statement: If $w$ is even with $w(0)>0$ then $\mu_0=\pi w(0)$ and the semicircle orthogonal polynomials exist uniquely.
items.note: Orthogonality on the semicircle (complex non-Hermitian inner product); complex-analytic, no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 1.71
items.statement: The zeros of the semicircle orthogonal polynomial $\pi_n(\cdot;w)$ are the eigenvalues of the associated complex tridiagonal matrix $J_n(w)$.
items.note: Orthogonality on the semicircle (complex non-Hermitian inner product); complex-analytic, no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 2.1
items.name: Determinantal formula
items.statement: $\pi_k(t)$ equals the Hankel determinant $\Delta_{k+1}$ with last row replaced by $(1,t,\dots,t^k)$, divided by $\Delta_k$; in particular its $t^{k-1}$ coefficient is $-\Delta_k'/\Delta_k$.
items.note: Candidate `hankel-moment-positivity`, priority later.

items.label: Thm 2.2
items.name: Recurrence coefficients from moments
items.statement: $\alpha_k=\Delta_{k+1}'/\Delta_{k+1}-\Delta_k'/\Delta_k$ and $\beta_k=\Delta_{k+1}\Delta_{k-1}/\Delta_k^2$.
items.note: Candidate `hankel-moment-positivity`.

items.label: Def 2.3
items.name: Absolute condition number (scalar)
items.statement: For $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ differentiable at $x$, $(\mathrm{cond}_{abs}f)(x)=\vert f'(x)\vert $.
items.note: Candidate `condition-number-of-map-def` (later); NLAlib has only the matrix condition number `condition-number-def`.

items.label: Def 2.4
items.name: Relative condition number (scalar)
items.statement: For $x\ne0$, $f(x)\ne0$: $(\mathrm{cond}_{rel}f)(x)=\vert xf'(x)/f(x)\vert $ (with a mollified variant switching to absolute errors for small quantities).
items.note: Candidate `condition-number-of-map-def`.

items.label: Def 2.5
items.name: Absolute condition number (vector)
items.statement: For $f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$ Fréchet differentiable at $x$, $(\mathrm{cond}_{abs}f)(x)=\Vert \partial f(x)/\partial x\Vert $ in a chosen matrix norm.
items.note: Candidate `condition-number-of-map-def`.

items.label: Def 2.6
items.name: Relative condition matrix
items.statement:
With $c_{
u\mu}=x_\mu(\partial f_
u/\partial x_\mu)/f_
u$, the relative condition number is $\Vert C(x)\Vert $ (componentwise relative sensitivities).
items.note: Candidate `condition-number-of-map-def`.

items.label: Thm 2.11
items.name: Ill-conditioning of moments → Gauss rule
items.statement:
For a measure on $\mathbb R_+$, the absolute condition number of the map from $\mu_0,\dots,\mu_{2n-1}$ to the Gauss nodes and weights is at least $\min(1,1/\max\lambda_
u)\,\pi_n(-1)^2/\min_
u(1+	au_
u)\pi_n'(	au_
u)^2$.
items.note: Numerical condition estimates for specific moment maps (confluent Vandermonde / Hermite-basis norms); NLAlib works in exact arithmetic and no randomized-NLA result cites them.

items.label: Thm 2.13
items.statement: The mollified relative condition number of the moment-to-Gauss-rule map is $\Vert C(\mu)\Vert $ with entries built from $T^{-1}$ (inverse confluent Vandermonde matrix) and the moments.
items.note: Numerical condition estimates for specific moment maps (confluent Vandermonde / Hermite-basis norms); NLAlib works in exact arithmetic and no randomized-NLA result cites them.

items.label: Thm 2.17
items.statement:
In the Frobenius norm, the absolute condition number of the map from normalised modified moments to the Gauss rule is $(\int g_n\,d\ell)^{1/2}$ with $g_n=\sum_
u[h_
u^2+\lambda_
u^{-2}k_
u^2]$ built from the Hermite basis at the Gauss nodes.
items.note: Numerical condition estimates for specific moment maps (confluent Vandermonde / Hermite-basis norms); NLAlib works in exact arithmetic and no randomized-NLA result cites them.

items.label: Thm 2.19
items.statement: The relative condition number of the modified-moment-to-Gauss-rule map is the norm of an explicit matrix $C(\tilde m)$ formed from the Hermite-basis coefficients.
items.note: Numerical condition estimates for specific moment maps (confluent Vandermonde / Hermite-basis norms); NLAlib works in exact arithmetic and no randomized-NLA result cites them.

items.label: Lem 2.21
items.statement: If $q\in\mathcal P_{2n-1}$ depends smoothly on the modified moments, $\partial_{m_k}\int q\,d\lambda=c_k[q]+\int\partial_{m_k}q\,d\lambda$, where $c_k[q]$ is the $k$th coefficient of $q$ in the basis $p_j$.
items.note: Candidate `recurrence-coefficient-moment-sensitivity` (later).

items.label: Thm 2.22
items.name: Derivatives of recurrence coefficients
items.statement: $\partial\alpha_j/\partial m_k=c_k[\tilde\psi_{2j+1}]$ and $\partial\beta_j/\partial m_k=c_k[\tilde\psi_{2j}]$ with $\tilde\psi_{2j}=\beta_j(\tilde\pi_j^2-\tilde\pi_{j-1}^2)$, $\tilde\psi_{2j+1}=\sqrt{\beta_{j+1}}\tilde\pi_j\tilde\pi_{j+1}-\sqrt{\beta_j}\tilde\pi_{j-1}\tilde\pi_j$.
items.note: Candidate `recurrence-coefficient-moment-sensitivity`.

items.label: Cor 1 to Thm 2.22
items.statement: The absolute condition number of the map from modified moments to recurrence coefficients is $\Vert \tilde\Psi\Vert $ with $\tilde\Psi_{lk}=c_k[\tilde\psi_l]$ (explicit in the $\infty$- and Frobenius norms).
items.note: Candidate `recurrence-coefficient-moment-sensitivity`.

items.label: Cor 2 to Thm 2.22
items.statement: The mollified relative condition number of that map is $\Vert C(m)\Vert $ with entries $m(m_k)\vert c_k[\tilde\psi]\vert /m(\alpha_j)$ resp. $/m(\beta_j)$.
items.note: Candidate `recurrence-coefficient-moment-sensitivity`.

items.label: Cor 3 to Thm 2.22
items.statement: The same condition number in terms of monic polynomials: $\tilde\psi_l=\psi_l$ with $\psi_{2j}=(\pi_j^2-\beta_j\pi_{j-1}^2)/(\beta_0\cdots\beta_{j-1})$ and $\psi_{2j+1}=(\pi_j\pi_{j+1}-\beta_j\pi_{j-1}\pi_j)/(\beta_0\cdots\beta_j)$.
items.note: Candidate `recurrence-coefficient-moment-sensitivity`.

items.label: Alg 2.1
items.name: Modified Chebyshev algorithm
items.statement: From $2n$ modified moments $m_k=\int p_k\,d\lambda$ (with $p_k$ satisfying a known three-term recurrence) the mixed moments $\sigma_{kl}=\int\pi_kp_l\,d\lambda$ obey a recursion that yields $\alpha_k,\beta_k$ for $k<n$.
items.note: Candidate `modified-chebyshev-algorithm` (moments → Jacobi matrix, as in KPM-to-Gauss spectral density methods).

items.label: Alg 2.2
items.name: Clenshaw's algorithm
items.statement: A finite sum $\sum_{j\le n}c_jy_j$ of solutions of a three-term recurrence is evaluated by a backward recurrence $u_k=c_k+(t-a_k)u_{k+1}-b_{k+1}u_{k+2}$.
items.note: Candidate `clenshaw-recurrence` (later).

items.label: Alg 2.3
items.name: Clenshaw for Chebyshev expansions
items.statement: Specialisation of Clenshaw's algorithm to $\sum c_jT_j(t)$.
items.note: Candidate `clenshaw-recurrence`.

items.label: Alg 2.4
items.name: Conversion algorithm
items.statement: Converts an expansion in one family of monic orthogonal polynomials into an expansion in another, given both recurrences.
items.note: Numerical basis-conversion procedure; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 2.32
items.name: Convergence of discretisations
items.statement: If discrete measures $d\lambda_N$ on $[-1,1]$ satisfy $(p,q)_{d\lambda_N}\to(p,q)_{d\lambda}$ for all polynomials, then $\alpha_{k,N}\to\alpha_k$, $\beta_{k,N}\to\beta_k$ and $\pi_n(\cdot;d\lambda_N)\to\pi_n(\cdot;d\lambda)$ uniformly on $[-1,1]$.
items.note: Candidate `recurrence-coefficient-continuity` (later).

items.label: Cor to Thm 2.32
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses the zeros of $\pi_{n,N}$ converge to those of $\pi_n$, and $\pi_{m,N}(\tau_{\nu,N})\to\pi_m(\tau_\nu)$.
items.note: Candidate `recurrence-coefficient-continuity`.

items.label: Sec 2.2.3.1
items.name: Stieltjes procedure
items.statement: For a discrete measure, alternate $\alpha_k=(t\pi_k,\pi_k)/(\pi_k,\pi_k)$, $\beta_k=(\pi_k,\pi_k)/(\pi_{k-1},\pi_{k-1})$ with the recurrence $\pi_{k+1}=(t-\alpha_k)\pi_k-\beta_k\pi_{k-1}$ evaluated at the nodes.
items.note: Unnumbered (indexed for its role). NLAlib has the matrix form (Lanczos on $(A,b)$ = Stieltjes on $\mu_b$), with the recursion-to-Arnoldi link a scaffold; the measure-side procedure on nodes and weights is not stated.

items.label: Sec 2.2.3.2
items.name: Lanczos-type algorithm for discrete measures
items.statement: With $D_t=\operatorname{diag}(t_\nu)$ and $\sqrt w$, an orthogonal $Q_1$ transforms $\begin{bmatrix}1&\sqrt w^\top\\\sqrt w&D_t\end{bmatrix}$ into $\begin{bmatrix}1&\sqrt{\beta_0}e_1^\top\\\sqrt{\beta_0}e_1&J_N(d\lambda_N)\end{bmatrix}$; Lanczos (stably: Gragg–Harrod rotations) computes it.
items.note: Unnumbered (indexed for its role). Lanczos on $(D_t,\sqrt w)$ gives $T_N=J_N(\mu_{\sqrt w})$ in NLAlib's setting; the bordered-matrix form and the identification of $\mu$ with the given discrete measure are not stated. Candidate `discrete-measure-jacobi-matrix`.

items.label: Thm 2.48
items.name: Contour-integral Gauss remainder
items.statement: For $f$ analytic on a domain containing $[a,b]$, $R_n^G(f)=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma K_n(z)f(z)\,dz$ with kernel $K_n=\rho_n/\pi_n$, $\rho_n(z)=\int\pi_n(t)\,d\lambda(t)/(z-t)$.
items.note: NLAlib bounds the analytic Gauss error via Chebyshev/Bernstein-ellipse approximation (`lanczos-quadrature-analytic-error`), not via this kernel. Candidate `gauss-remainder-contour-kernel` (later).

items.label: Thm 2.52
items.name: Uvarov (generalised Christoffel), m ≤ n
items.statement: For $d\hat\lambda=(u/v)\,d\lambda$ with $u,v$ coprime with simple zeros, $\deg v=m\le n$, $u\,\pi_n(\cdot;d\hat\lambda)$ is a determinant in $\pi_{n-m},\dots,\pi_{n+\ell}$ and their values at zeros of $u$ and Cauchy integrals $\rho_k$ at zeros of $v$.
items.note: Candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification` (later). The case $m=0$ is Christoffel's theorem.

items.label: Thm 2.53
items.name: Uvarov, m > n
items.statement: The analogous determinantal formula for $u\,\pi_n(\cdot;d\hat\lambda)$ when $\deg v=m>n$, with a block of powers of the zeros of $v$.
items.note: Candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification`.

items.label: Alg 2.5
items.name: Modification by a linear factor
items.statement: Recurrence coefficients of $(t-z)\,d\lambda$ from those of $d\lambda$: $r_{k+1}=z-\alpha_{k+1}-\beta_{k+1}/r_k$, $\hat\alpha_k=\alpha_{k+1}+r_{k+1}-r_k$, $\hat\beta_k=\beta_kr_k/r_{k-1}$, $\hat\beta_0=-r_0\beta_0$.
items.note: Algorithmic form of Thm 1.55/1.57; candidate `kernel-polynomials-christoffel`.

items.label: Alg 2.6
items.name: Modification by a quadratic factor
items.statement: Recurrence coefficients of $((t-x)^2+y^2)\,d\lambda$ from those of $d\lambda$.
items.note: Numerical modification algorithm for quadratic factors or rational divisors; grouped in candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification` (later).

items.label: Alg 2.7
items.name: Simplified symmetric quadratic factor
items.statement: Recurrence coefficients of $(t^2+y^2)\,d\lambda$ for symmetric $d\lambda$.
items.note: Numerical modification algorithm for quadratic factors or rational divisors; grouped in candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification` (later).

items.label: Alg 2.8
items.name: Modification by a linear divisor
items.statement: Recurrence coefficients of $d\lambda/(t-z)$ via Cauchy integrals $\rho_k(z)$.
items.note: Numerical modification algorithm for quadratic factors or rational divisors; grouped in candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification` (later).

items.label: Lem 2.54
items.statement: For $d\hat\lambda=d\lambda/((t-x)^2+y^2)$, $\hat\pi_n=\pi_n+s_n\pi_{n-1}+t_n\pi_{n-2}$ with $s_n,t_n$ explicit in the real and imaginary parts of $r_k=\rho_{k+1}(z)/\rho_k(z)$.
items.note: Candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification`.

items.label: Alg 2.9
items.name: Modification by a quadratic divisor
items.statement: Recurrence coefficients of $d\lambda/((t-x)^2+y^2)$.
items.note: Numerical modification algorithm for quadratic factors or rational divisors; grouped in candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification` (later).

items.label: Alg 2.10
items.name: Simplified symmetric quadratic divisor
items.statement: Recurrence coefficients of $d\lambda/(t^2+y^2)$ for symmetric $d\lambda$.
items.note: Numerical modification algorithm for quadratic factors or rational divisors; grouped in candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification` (later).

items.label: Lem 2.55
items.statement: For the special quadratic divisor $d\lambda/(t^2-x^2)$, $\hat\pi_n=\pi_n+s_n\pi_{n-1}+t_n\pi_{n-2}$ with $s_n,t_n$ explicit in $r_k^\pm$.
items.note: Candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification`.

items.label: Alg 2.11
items.name: Special quadratic divisor
items.statement: Recurrence coefficients of $d\lambda/(t^2-x^2)$ from those of $d\lambda$.
items.note: Numerical modification algorithm for quadratic factors or rational divisors; grouped in candidate `christoffel-uvarov-modification` (later).

items.label: Thm 3.1
items.name: Golub–Welsch
items.statement: The $n$-point Gauss nodes are the eigenvalues of $J_n(d\lambda)$ and the weights are $\beta_0v_{\nu,1}^2$ (squared first eigenvector components); hence the Gauss sum is $\beta_0e_1^\top f(J_n)e_1$.
items.note: Proved in full for $\mu_b$ (eigenpairs of $T_q$ give a rule exact to degree $2q-1$; the sum is $\Vert b\Vert ^2e_1^\top f(T_q)e_1$). NLAlib states it only for the spectral measure $\mu_b$ of a symmetric matrix and a vector (finitely supported; every finitely supported positive measure is one, via $A=\operatorname{diag}(t)$, $b=\sqrt w$); the statement for a general positive measure on $\mathbb R$ with finite moments is missing.

items.label: Cor to Thm 3.1
items.name: Extended Jacobi matrix
items.statement: There is an orthogonal $Q$ with $\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&Q^\top\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&\sqrt{\lambda^G}^\top\\\sqrt{\lambda^G}&D_\tau\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&Q\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&\sqrt{\beta_0}e_1^\top\\\sqrt{\beta_0}e_1&J_n\end{bmatrix}$ ($Q=V^\top$).
items.note: The eigendecomposition of $T_q$ with first components $\sqrt{w_i}$ is there; the bordered-matrix (inverse eigenvalue) statement is not. Candidate `discrete-measure-jacobi-matrix`.

items.label: Thm 3.2
items.name: Gauss–Radau via Jacobi–Radau matrix
items.statement: Bordering $J_n$ with $\sqrt{\beta_n}e_n$ and the corner $\alpha_n^R=a-\beta_n\pi_{n-1}(a)/\pi_n(a)$ gives a matrix whose eigenvalues are the Gauss–Radau nodes (including $a$) and whose squared first eigenvector components times $\beta_0$ are the weights.
items.note: Candidate `gauss-radau-lobatto`.

items.label: Thm 3.3
items.name: Sign of the Radau remainder
items.statement: On a finite support $[a,b]$ with $f\in C^{2n+1}$ and $f^{(2n+1)}$ of constant sign, the left and right Gauss–Radau remainders have opposite, determined signs: one rule gives a lower and the other an upper bound.
items.note: Candidate `gauss-radau-lobatto`.

items.label: Thm 3.6
items.name: Gauss–Lobatto via Jacobi–Lobatto matrix
items.statement: Bordering $J_{n+1}$ with $\sqrt{\beta_{n+1}^L}e_{n+1}$ and corner $\alpha_{n+1}^L$, where $(\alpha^L,\beta^L)$ solve a $2\times2$ system in $\pi_n,\pi_{n+1}$ at $a,b$, gives the Gauss–Lobatto nodes (with $a,b$) and weights by Golub–Welsch.
items.note: Candidate `gauss-radau-lobatto`.

items.label: Thm 3.7
items.name: Sign of the Lobatto remainder
items.statement: If $f\in C^{2n+2}[a,b]$ and $f^{(2n+2)}>0$ there, the Gauss–Lobatto remainder is negative (reversed for the opposite sign).
items.note: Candidate `gauss-radau-lobatto`.

items.label: Thm 3.9
items.name: Generalised Gauss–Radau
items.statement: The interior nodes/weights of the Gauss–Radau rule with an $r$-fold end point $a$ are the Gauss nodes of $(t-a)^r d\lambda$ with weights divided by $(\tau_\nu-a)^r$; all positive.
items.note: Multiple end-point quadrature for ODE/spline applications; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.12
items.name: Generalised Gauss–Lobatto
items.statement: The interior nodes/weights of the Gauss–Lobatto rule with $r$-fold end points are the Gauss nodes of $[(t-a)(b-t)]^rd\lambda$ with weights divided by $[(\tau-a)(b-\tau)]^r$.
items.note: Multiple end-point quadrature; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.15
items.name: Stieltjes polynomial
items.statement: For a positive measure, the Stieltjes polynomial of degree $n+1$ (orthogonal to $\mathcal P_n$ against $\pi_n\,d\lambda$) exists uniquely.
items.note: Gauss–Kronrod extension theory; no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Lem 3.17
items.name: Laurie's Kronrod matrix lemma
items.statement: In the Jacobi–Kronrod matrix, the trailing block $J_n^*$ has the same eigenvalues as $J_n(d\lambda)$.
items.note: Gauss–Kronrod construction; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.20
items.statement: For a symmetric measure, Gauss–Turán nodes are symmetric and the weights satisfy $\lambda_{n+1-\nu}^{(\sigma)}=(-1)^\sigma\lambda_\nu^{(\sigma)}$.
items.note: Gauss–Turán (derivative) quadrature; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.25
items.name: Rational Gauss quadrature
items.statement: If $d\lambda/\omega_m$, $\omega_m=\prod(1+\zeta_\mu t)^{s_\mu}$, has an $n$-point Gauss rule with nodes in $[a,b]$, then the same nodes with weights $\lambda_\nu^G\omega_m(\tau_\nu)$ integrate exactly the $2n$-dimensional space of rational functions with the prescribed poles plus $\mathcal P_{2n-1-m}$; and conversely.
items.note: Candidate `rational-gauss-quadrature` (later; consumer: rational Krylov methods for $f(A)b$).

items.label: Thm 3.39
items.name: Rational Gauss–Radau
items.statement: If $d\lambda/\omega_m$ admits a polynomial Gauss–Radau rule, rescaling its weights by $\omega_m$ at the nodes gives a rule exact on the corresponding space of rational functions with prescribed poles.
items.note: Rational variants of Radau/Lobatto/Kronrod/Turán rules; no consumer beyond `rational-gauss-quadrature`.

items.label: Thm 3.40
items.name: Rational Gauss–Lobatto
items.statement: If $d\lambda/\omega_m$ admits a polynomial Gauss–Lobatto rule, rescaling its weights by $\omega_m$ at the nodes gives a rule exact on the corresponding space of rational functions with prescribed poles.
items.note: Rational variants of Radau/Lobatto/Kronrod/Turán rules; no consumer beyond `rational-gauss-quadrature`.

items.label: Thm 3.41
items.name: Rational Gauss–Kronrod
items.statement: If $d\lambda/\omega_m$ admits a polynomial Gauss–Kronrod rule, rescaling its weights by $\omega_m$ at the nodes gives a rule exact on the corresponding space of rational functions with prescribed poles.
items.note: Rational variants of Radau/Lobatto/Kronrod/Turán rules; no consumer beyond `rational-gauss-quadrature`.

items.label: Thm 3.43
items.name: Rational Gauss–Turán
items.statement: If $d\lambda/\omega_m$ admits a polynomial Gauss–Turán rule, rescaling its weights by $\omega_m$ at the nodes gives a rule exact on the corresponding space of rational functions with prescribed poles.
items.note: Rational variants of Radau/Lobatto/Kronrod/Turán rules; no consumer beyond `rational-gauss-quadrature`.

items.label: Alg 3.1
items.name: Stieltjes procedure on several intervals
items.statement: Discretise a measure supported on several intervals by Gauss rules on each piece and run the Stieltjes procedure on the union.
items.note: Discretisation procedure for multi-interval weights; no consumer.

items.label: Alg 3.2
items.name: Modified moments on several intervals
items.statement: Compute the first $2n$ Chebyshev modified moments of a multi-interval measure.
items.note: Numerical procedure; no consumer.

items.label: Sec 3.1.7
items.name: Matrix functionals as integrals
items.statement: For symmetric $A$ with eigenpairs $(\lambda_k,v_k)$ and $u=\sum\rho_kv_k$, $u^\top f(A)u=\sum\rho_k^2f(\lambda_k)=\int f\,d\rho_N$, a discrete measure on the spectrum; $u^\top f(A)v$ follows by polarisation.
items.note: Unnumbered, eq. (3.1.143) (indexed for its role). Polarisation is not stated separately.

items.label: Alg 3.3
items.name: Lanczos algorithm
items.statement: $\alpha_j=h_j^\top Ah_j$, $\tilde h_{j+1}=(A-\alpha_j)h_j-\gamma_jh_{j-1}$, $\gamma_{j+1}=\Vert \tilde h_{j+1}\Vert $; the Lanczos vectors are orthonormal, span the Krylov spaces, and $h_j=p_j(A)h_0$ with $p_j$ the orthonormal polynomials of the spectral measure of $h_0$ ($\gamma_j=\sqrt{\beta_j}$).
items.note: The recursion-equals-Arnoldi link `lanczosRecurrence_eq_arnoldiBasis` is a scaffold (assumed); the polynomial and orthonormality facts are proved.

items.label: Example 3.46
items.name: Error bounds for linear systems
items.statement: For SPD $A$ and residual $r=b-Ax^*$, $\Vert x-x^*\Vert ^2=r^\top A^{-2}r$ and $\Vert x-x^*\Vert _A^2=r^\top A^{-1}r$ are integrals against the spectral measure of $r$; Gauss gives lower bounds, left Radau and Lobatto upper bounds, right Radau a lower bound.
items.note: Candidate `gauss-radau-lobatto` (with `gauss-quadrature-derivative-remainder`).

items.label: Example 3.47
items.name: Diagonal of the inverse
items.statement: For SPD $A$, $(A^{-1})_{ii}=e_i^\top A^{-1}e_i$ is bounded below by $e_1^\top J_n^{-1}e_1$ from Lanczos started at $e_i$, and two-sided by Radau/Lobatto rules; with $n=2$ the bound is explicit in the entries of $A$.
items.note: Candidate `gauss-radau-lobatto`; consumer `diagonal-estimator`.

items.label: Alg 3.4
items.name: Polynomial least squares
items.statement: Least-squares polynomial approximation on a discrete point set via the discrete orthogonal polynomials and Clenshaw evaluation.
items.note: Discrete least-squares data fitting; NLAlib's least squares is matrix least squares.

items.label: Alg 3.5
items.name: Sobolev least squares
items.statement: Least-squares approximation in a discrete Sobolev norm via Sobolev orthogonal polynomials.
items.note: Sobolev inner products (no shift property); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.54
items.statement: A step-function approximation on $\mathbb R_+$ with $n$ knots matching the first $2n$ moments of $f$ exists uniquely iff $-tf'(t)\,dt$ has an $n$-point Gauss rule with positive nodes; the knots are the Gauss nodes.
items.note: Moment-preserving spline approximation (physics application); no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.56
items.name: Moment-matching Dirac approximation
items.statement: For $f\ge0$ with $2n$ moments, the $n$-atom measure $\sum a_\nu\delta_{t_\nu}$ matching the first $2n$ moments of $f\,dt$ is unique and is the $n$-point Gauss rule of $f\,dt$.
items.note: Uniqueness of the moment-matching $n$-atom measure (Lanczos quadrature as moment matching). Candidate `quadrature-exactness-characterisation`.

items.label: Thm 3.57
items.statement: Spline approximation of degree $m$ with $n$ knots matching $2n$ moments exists uniquely iff $\frac{(-1)^{m+1}}{m!}t^{m+1}f^{(m+1)}(t)\,dt$ admits an $n$-point Gauss rule with positive nodes.
items.note: Moment-preserving spline approximation (physics application); no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.58
items.statement: The error of the moment-preserving spline at $t$ equals the Gauss remainder of the truncated power $s^{-(m+1)}(s-t)_+^m$ for the measure of Theorem 3.57.
items.note: Moment-preserving spline approximation (physics application); no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.61
items.statement: On $[0,1]$, moment-preserving spline Problem I has a unique solution iff $\frac{(-1)^{m+1}}{m!}f^{(m+1)}dt$ admits a generalised Gauss–Lobatto rule with interior nodes in $(0,1)$.
items.note: Moment-preserving spline approximation (physics application); no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 3.62
items.statement: On $[0,1]$, Problem II has a unique solution iff that measure admits a generalised Gauss–Radau rule with interior nodes in $(0,1)$.
items.note: Moment-preserving spline approximation (physics application); no NLA consumer.
